name: Band Seated Row
steps: Sit tall on the floor with legs extended, knees slightly bent, and loop the middle of the band around the soles of your feet.
Hold one end in each hand, palms facing each other, arms straight and the band lightly taut.
Pull your elbows back close to your ribs, squeezing your shoulder blades together, until your hands reach your lower ribs.
Pause for a second, then let your arms straighten slowly without rounding your back or shrugging.

name: Band Bent-Over Row
steps: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand.
Soften your knees and hinge at the hips until your torso is about 45 degrees to the floor, back flat and neck neutral.
Row your hands toward your lower ribs, driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Lower under control to straight arms while holding the hinge.

name: Band Single-Arm Row
steps: Anchor the band at about chest height, hold the free end in one hand and step back until it is taut.
Take a staggered stance with the opposite foot forward, knees soft and chest tall.
Row your hand to the side of your ribs, keeping the elbow close and the shoulder blade sliding back and down, without twisting your torso.
Return slowly to a straight arm, letting the shoulder blade glide forward a little at the end.

name: Band Face Pull
steps: Anchor the band at face height, hold an end in each hand with palms facing down and step back until the band is taut.
Pull the band toward your forehead, leading with high, wide elbows and separating your hands as you pull.
Finish with your hands beside your ears and knuckles pointing up, squeezing the back of your shoulders without arching your lower back.
Return slowly to straight arms.

name: Band Diagonal Pull-Apart
steps: Hold a light band in front of your chest with straight arms and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the band apart on a diagonal: one hand travels up and out above shoulder height while the other goes down and out toward the opposite hip.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end without letting your ribs flare, then return slowly.
Alternate which hand goes high each rep or each set.

name: Band Overhead Pull-Apart
steps: Hold a light band overhead with straight arms, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and ribs drawn down.
Pull the band apart as you lower it behind your head toward your upper back, keeping the arms long.
Stop when your hands reach shoulder height, or sooner if you feel any pinching, then return overhead with control.

name: Band External Rotation at 90° Abduction
steps: Anchor the band at shoulder height, face it and hold the end in one hand.
Lift the upper arm out to shoulder height, slightly in front of your body, with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the forearm pointing toward the anchor.
Keeping the elbow at the same height, rotate the forearm up until it points to the ceiling, without arching your back or shrugging.
Lower slowly back to the start; use a light band and stay in a pain-free range.

name: Band Internal Rotation at 90° Abduction
steps: Anchor the band at shoulder height behind you and hold the end in one hand, facing away from the anchor.
Raise the upper arm to shoulder height, slightly in front of your body, with the elbow bent to 90 degrees and the forearm pointing up.
Rotate the forearm forward and down until it is parallel to the floor, keeping the elbow in place.
Return slowly to vertical, controlling the band the whole way.

name: Band Bilateral External Rotation
steps: Hold a light band with both hands, palms up, elbows bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your sides.
Rotate your forearms outward to stretch the band, keeping the elbows pinned to your ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down at the end range, then return slowly.

name: Band Y Raise
steps: Anchor a light band low in front of you or stand on its middle, holding an end in each hand with thumbs pointing up.
With straight arms, raise your hands up and out into a Y shape, about 30 degrees wide of vertical.
Lift only as high as you can without shrugging or arching your lower back, keeping the shoulder blades drawn down.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Band Bent-Over T Raise
steps: Stand on the middle of a light band, cross the ends so each hand holds the opposite side, and hinge forward with a flat back.
Let your arms hang below your shoulders with thumbs pointing forward.
Raise your straight arms out to the sides to form a T, squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly without losing the hinge position.

name: Band W Raise
steps: Anchor a light band at chest height, hold an end in each hand and face the anchor with arms reaching forward.
Pull your elbows down and back toward your ribs while rotating your hands outward so your arms form a W.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down at the end, keeping your neck relaxed.
Reach forward slowly to return.

name: Band Scapular Retraction
steps: Anchor the band at chest height, hold an end in each hand with straight arms and step back until it is lightly taut.
Without bending your elbows, draw your shoulder blades back and together so your hands travel a few centimetres toward you.
Hold for two seconds, then let the shoulder blades glide forward slowly.

name: Band Serratus Punch
steps: Anchor the band at chest height behind you, hold the end in one hand and step forward until it is taut.
Press your hand straight forward until the elbow is fully extended.
Keeping the elbow straight, reach a few centimetres further by letting the shoulder blade glide forward around your rib cage.
Draw the shoulder blade back, then bend the arm slowly to return.

name: Band D2 Shoulder Flexion
steps: Anchor the band low on the side opposite your working arm and hold it with that hand near the opposite hip, palm facing your body.
Pull the band up and across your body, turning the thumb outward as the arm finishes above your head on the working side, like drawing a sword.
Keep your trunk tall and ribs down, finishing with the arm in line with your shoulder blade rather than behind your head.
Return along the same diagonal slowly.

name: Band Standing Chest Press
steps: Anchor the band at chest height behind you, hold an end in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance until the band is taut.
Start with your hands beside your chest and elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press your hands forward until your arms are straight, keeping your core braced and torso still.
Return slowly until your hands are back beside your chest.

name: Band Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Press
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, anchor the band under the down knee and hold the free end at shoulder height on that same side.
Squeeze the glute of the down leg and brace your core so your ribs stay stacked over your pelvis.
Press your hand straight overhead until the arm is beside your ear, without leaning or arching.
Lower slowly to shoulder height, and switch sides after the set.

name: Band Low-to-High Chest Fly
steps: Anchor the band low behind you, or stand on it in a staggered stance, and hold an end in each hand beside your hips, palms facing forward.
With a slight bend in the elbows, sweep your hands forward and up in an arc until they meet at about chin height.
Squeeze your chest at the top, then lower slowly along the same arc.

name: Band Biceps Curl
steps: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl your hands up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to fully straight arms.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
steps: Anchor the band high, for example over a door, and hold an end in each hand while facing the anchor.
Start with your elbows bent and tucked at your sides, hands at chest height.
Push your hands down until your arms are straight, spreading them slightly apart at the bottom.
Let the hands rise back to chest height slowly without letting the elbows drift forward.

name: Band Triceps Kickback
steps: Stand on the middle of the band, hold an end in each hand and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back.
Lift your elbows beside your ribs so the upper arms are parallel to your torso and the elbows are bent to 90 degrees.
Straighten your elbows to push your hands back, keeping the upper arms still.
Bend the elbows slowly to return.

name: Band Kneeling Lat Pulldown
steps: Anchor the band high above you and kneel facing it, holding an end in each hand with arms straight overhead.
Draw your shoulder blades down first, then pull your elbows down toward your sides until your hands are near your shoulders.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning back; pause briefly at the bottom.
Let your arms return overhead with control.

name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
steps: Anchor the band high, hold an end in each hand and step back so your arms are straight in front of you at about eye level.
Hinge slightly at the hips and brace your core.
Keeping your elbows straight, sweep your hands down to your thighs by squeezing your lats.
Return slowly to eye level without shrugging.

name: Band Wrist Flexion
steps: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing up and the hand hanging just past the knee.
Stand on one end of a light band and hold the other end in your hand with a little tension.
Curl your wrist up as far as is comfortable, keeping the forearm flat on your thigh.
Lower slowly over about three seconds, emphasising the lowering phase.

name: Band Wrist Extension
steps: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh, palm facing down and the hand hanging just past the knee.
Stand on one end of a light band and hold the other end so there is slight tension.
Lift the back of your hand up as far as is comfortable while the forearm stays flat.
Lower slowly over about three seconds; slow lowering is a staple of tennis elbow rehab.

name: Band Forearm Pronation
steps: Sit with your forearm on your thigh, elbow bent to 90 degrees and palm facing up.
Grip one end of a light band so it leaves your hand on the thumb side and runs down to your foot on the outside, which pins the other end.
Rotate your forearm until the palm faces down, keeping the elbow still and close to your side.
Rotate back slowly to palm up.

name: Band Forearm Supination
steps: Sit with your forearm on your thigh, elbow bent to 90 degrees and palm facing down.
Grip one end of a light band so it leaves your hand on the little-finger side and runs down to your foot on the outside, which pins the other end.
Rotate your forearm until the palm faces up, keeping the elbow still and close to your side.
Return slowly to palm down.

name: Band Radial Deviation
steps: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh, thumb pointing up and the wrist just past your knee.
Hold a light band in your fist with the other end pinned under your foot directly below.
Without moving the forearm, tilt your hand up toward the thumb side as far as is comfortable.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Band Ulnar Deviation
steps: Stand tall with your arm by your side and thumb pointing forward, holding one end of a light band with the other end under your foot slightly in front of you.
Keeping the elbow straight and the arm still, tilt your hand backward toward the little-finger side.
Pause, then return slowly to neutral.

name: Rubber Band Finger Extension
steps: Loop a rubber band around the outside of all five fingertips with the fingers gathered together.
Spread your fingers and thumb as wide as you can against the band.
Hold the open position for a second, then close slowly.

name: Band Deadlift
steps: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand beside your shins.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower your hands toward your shins, keeping your back flat and chest proud.
Drive through your whole foot to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top without leaning back.
Hinge back down under control.

name: Band Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand on the band with feet hip-width apart, holding the ends in front of your thighs with straight arms.
With a soft bend in the knees, push your hips back and slide your hands down your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually just below the knees, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.

name: Band Split Squat
steps: Take a long split stance with the band under your front foot and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Lower straight down until the back knee hovers just above the floor, torso tall and front knee tracking over the toes.
Push through the front heel and midfoot to rise, completing all reps before switching legs.

name: Banded Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, and a mini band just above your knees.
Press your knees gently out against the band and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes for a second at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower slowly and repeat.

name: Band Hip Thrust
steps: Sit with your upper back against a sturdy bench or couch and a band across your hips, its ends anchored under heavy dumbbells or the bench legs on each side.
Plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart, so your shins will be vertical at the top.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is level with the floor, chin tucked and ribs down.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.

name: Band Clamshell
steps: Lie on your side with a mini band just above your knees, hips and knees bent to about 45 degrees and heels together.
Keeping your feet touching and your pelvis stacked, lift your top knee as high as you can without rolling your hips back.
Pause, then lower slowly.

name: Band Lateral Walk
steps: Place a mini band around your legs just above the knees or around the ankles and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Sit into a quarter squat with your chest up and weight in your heels.
Step sideways with the lead foot, then follow with the trailing foot without letting the feet snap together or the knees cave in.
Take the set number of steps in one direction, then return leading with the other leg.

name: Band Quadruped Kickback
steps: Set up on hands and knees with a band looped around the sole of one foot and the ends held under your hands.
Brace your core so your back stays flat, then push the banded foot back and up until the hip is fully extended.
Squeeze the glute without arching your lower back or rotating your hips, then return slowly.

name: Band Standing Hip Abduction
steps: Stand tall next to a support with a mini band around your ankles, or a long band anchored low on your standing-leg side and looped around the working ankle.
Shift your weight onto the standing leg and keep your pelvis level.
Lift the working leg out to the side with the toes pointing forward, stopping before your torso tilts.
Lower slowly without letting the foot rest.

name: Band Standing Hip Adduction
steps: Anchor a band low, loop it around the ankle nearest the anchor and step away until there is tension.
Stand tall beside a support with the banded leg slightly out to the side.
Sweep the banded leg across in front of the standing leg, keeping the knee straight and hips square.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Band Lying Leg Press
steps: Lie on your back, draw one knee toward your chest and loop the middle of the band around the sole of that foot, holding the ends in your hands.
Keep your elbows pinned to the floor so the band stays anchored.
Press the foot away at about 45 degrees until the knee is straight.
Bend the knee back toward your chest slowly.

name: Band Prone Hamstring Curl
steps: Anchor a band low, for example around a heavy table leg, and lie face down with your feet toward the anchor and the loop around your ankles.
Slide away from the anchor until the band is taut with your legs straight.
Keeping your hips pressed into the floor, curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to straight legs.

name: Band Terminal Knee Extension
steps: Anchor a band at knee height and step into it so the loop sits behind one knee while you face the anchor.
Step back until the band pulls the knee into a slight bend, heel down.
Straighten the knee fully by squeezing your quad, pushing back against the band.
Hold for a second, then let the knee bend slowly.

name: Band Ankle Eversion
steps: Sit with your leg straight and loop a light band around the outside of your forefoot, anchoring the other end to the inside, such as around your other foot.
Keeping your knee and leg still, turn the sole of your foot outward against the band.
Pause, then return slowly to neutral.

name: Band Ankle Inversion
steps: Sit with your leg straight and loop a light band around the inside of your forefoot, anchoring the other end to the outside, such as a table leg.
Keeping your knee and leg still, turn the sole of your foot inward against the band.
Pause, then return slowly to neutral.

name: Band Pallof Press
steps: Anchor the band at chest height, stand side-on to the anchor and hold the end with both hands at your sternum, stepping out until the band is taut.
Set your feet hip-width apart with soft knees and brace your core.
Press your hands straight out from your chest without letting your torso rotate toward the anchor.
Hold for two seconds, bring your hands back to your chest, and finish the set before facing the other way.

name: Band Anti-Rotation Hold
steps: Stand side-on to a chest-height anchor with the band held at your sternum and step out until it pulls firmly.
Press your hands straight out and hold them in line with your sternum.
Breathe steadily while keeping hips and shoulders square; do not let the band rotate you.

name: Band High-to-Low Woodchop
steps: Anchor the band high on one side and hold the end with both hands above the shoulder nearest the anchor, arms long.
Stand side-on with feet wider than hips and knees soft.
Pull the band diagonally down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating through your hips and pivoting your back foot.
Control the return along the same diagonal.

name: Band Low-to-High Woodchop
steps: Anchor the band low on one side and hold the end with both hands beside the hip nearest the anchor, knees bent.
Rotate and rise, pulling the band up and across your body to finish above the opposite shoulder with arms long.
Let your hips and back foot pivot so the rotation is shared, not forced from the lower back.
Return slowly along the same path.

name: Band Forehand Rotation
steps: Anchor the band at waist height on your racket-hand side, slightly behind you, and hold the end with both hands as if preparing for a forehand.
Load into your back hip with your shoulders turned toward the anchor.
Drive from the back leg and rotate hips then trunk forward, pulling the band across your body until your chest faces forward.
Return slowly to the loaded position; keep the arms fairly passive so the hips and trunk do the work.

name: Band Backhand Rotation
steps: Anchor the band at waist height on your non-racket side, slightly behind you, and hold the end with both hands as if preparing for a backhand.
Turn your shoulders toward the anchor with your weight loaded into the back leg.
Step and rotate through hips and trunk, sweeping the band across and up to a high finish over your racket-side shoulder.
Return slowly; also train the opposite direction for balance.

name: Band Kneeling Crunch
steps: Anchor the band high, kneel facing it and hold the ends beside your head with elbows bent.
Keeping your hips still, curl your ribs toward your pelvis, bringing your elbows toward your thighs.
Exhale fully at the bottom, then slowly uncurl to the start without letting the band pull your hips back.

name: Band Dead Bug
steps: Anchor the band low behind your head and lie on your back holding it with straight arms above your chest, pulling it toward your hips to create tension.
Lift your knees to 90 degrees over your hips and press your lower back gently into the floor.
Slowly extend one leg until it hovers above the floor while your arms keep the band pulled down, then return.
Alternate legs, keeping your lower back in contact with the floor throughout.

name: Band Resisted Sprint
steps: Loop a heavy band around your waist and anchor it securely behind you, or have a partner hold it.
Lean forward from the ankles and drive your knees with quick, powerful steps against the band.
Sprint for the set time, stopping before the band reaches full stretch, then walk back and rest fully between efforts.

name: Band Resisted Lateral Shuffle
steps: Loop a band around your waist with the anchor to one side, then step away until it pulls firmly.
Set an athletic stance with feet wider than hips, knees bent and chest up.
Shuffle away from the anchor with quick, low steps without crossing your feet, then control the shuffle back.
Complete the time on one side, then turn around so the band pulls from the other direction.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
steps: From hands and knees, tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back so your body forms an inverted V.
Spread your fingers wide, press through the whole hand and rotate your upper arms outward to make space around your neck.
Lengthen your spine first, bending the knees as much as needed, then work the heels toward the floor.
Breathe slowly and let your head hang between your arms.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
steps: Lie face down with the tops of your feet on the mat and your hands beside your lower ribs.
Press into your hands and the tops of your feet to straighten your arms, lifting your chest, hips and thighs off the floor.
Draw your shoulders back and down away from your ears and keep your legs active.
Hold for a few breaths, then lower down or press back to Downward-Facing Dog.

name: Cobra Pose
steps: Lie face down with legs extended, tops of the feet down and hands under your shoulders, elbows tucked in.
Press your pubic bone and feet into the mat and peel your chest off the floor using your back muscles, with only light pressure through your hands.
Keep your elbows bent and the back of your neck long, lifting only as high as is comfortable for your lower back.
Lower slowly on an exhale.

name: Sphinx Pose
steps: Lie face down and prop yourself up on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders.
Press your forearms down to lift your chest, drawing your shoulders away from your ears.
Relax your glutes and let your lower back settle into a gentle extension while you breathe steadily.

name: Extended Child's Pose
steps: Kneel with big toes touching and knees about mat-width apart, then sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest between your thighs, resting your forehead on the mat or a block.
Reach actively through your fingertips to lengthen the sides of your body, then soften and breathe into your back.

name: Mountain Pose
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart, weight spread evenly between heels and the balls of your feet.
Gently firm your thighs, lengthen your tailbone down and stack your ribs over your pelvis.
Roll your shoulders back and down with arms by your sides, palms facing forward, and lengthen through the crown of your head.
Breathe evenly and hold still.

name: Chair Pose
steps: Stand with feet together or hip-width apart and raise your arms overhead.
Bend your knees and sit your hips back as if lowering into a chair, keeping your weight in your heels.
Lengthen your spine and draw your ribs in rather than arching your lower back.
Hold for several breaths, then press through your feet to stand.

name: Warrior I
steps: From standing, step one foot back about a leg's length and turn the back foot out about 45 degrees, heel down.
Square your hips toward the front as much as is comfortable and bend your front knee over the ankle.
Raise your arms overhead with your shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Hold while breathing steadily, then switch sides.

name: Warrior II
steps: Stand with feet wide, turn the front foot to point forward and the back foot slightly in.
Bend the front knee until it is over the ankle, tracking toward the little-toe side of the foot.
Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height and gaze over your front hand.
Keep your torso upright over your pelvis, then switch sides.

name: Warrior III
steps: From a high lunge, shift your weight onto the front foot and hinge forward.
Lift the back leg until it is roughly level with your hips, keeping your hips square to the floor.
Reach your arms forward or rest your hands on your hips so your body forms a T from fingertips to back heel.
Hold with a soft standing knee, then step down and switch sides.

name: Extended Side Angle Pose
steps: From Warrior II, lower your front forearm onto your front thigh, or your front hand to a block outside the foot.
Extend your top arm over your ear so there is one long line from the back heel to the fingertips.
Press your front knee toward the little-toe side and rotate your chest toward the ceiling.
Hold, then return to Warrior II and switch sides.

name: Triangle Pose
steps: Stand with feet wide, front foot pointing forward and back foot turned slightly in, both legs straight but not locked.
Reach forward over your front leg, then tilt your torso and rest the lower hand on your shin, a block or the floor.
Extend your top arm toward the ceiling and open your chest, keeping both sides of the waist long.
Hold, rise with control and switch sides.

name: Revolved Triangle Pose
steps: Stand with feet about a leg's length apart, hips square to the front leg and the back foot angled out.
Hinge forward with a long spine and place the hand opposite your front leg on a block or the floor beside the front foot.
Rotate your chest toward the front leg and reach the other arm up, turning from your middle back rather than forcing your neck.
Hold, return to standing and switch sides.

name: Pyramid Pose
steps: Step one foot back about a metre, keep both legs straight and turn the back foot slightly out with your hips facing forward.
Lengthen your spine, then hinge at the hips to fold over the front leg, hands on blocks or your shin.
Keep your back flat rather than rounding to reach lower, and press evenly through both feet.
Hold, then rise with a long spine and switch sides.

name: Tree Pose
steps: Stand on one leg and place the sole of the other foot on your inner ankle, calf or upper thigh, avoiding the side of the knee.
Press the foot and standing leg into each other and keep your hips level.
Bring your hands to your chest or reach them overhead while gazing at a fixed point.
Hold, then switch sides.

name: Low Lunge
steps: From a lunge, lower your back knee to the mat, padding it if needed, with your front knee stacked over the ankle.
Lift your torso upright and raise your arms overhead.
Gently tuck your tailbone and shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip, without arching your lower back.
Hold, then switch sides.

name: High Lunge
steps: Step one foot back into a long lunge with the back heel lifted and the front knee over the ankle.
Lift your torso upright and reach your arms overhead.
Straighten the back leg by pressing out through the heel, and draw the front hip back to keep your hips square.
Hold, then switch sides.

name: Lizard Pose
steps: From a low lunge, place both hands inside your front foot and step that foot toward the edge of the mat.
Lower your back knee to the floor and let your hips sink forward and down.
Stay on your hands, or lower to your forearms on blocks or the floor if your hips allow.
Hold with steady breathing, then switch sides.

name: Pigeon Pose
steps: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind the same wrist and angle the shin across the mat so the foot is in front of the opposite hip.
Slide the back leg straight behind you and keep your hips as level as possible, with a cushion under the front hip if needed.
Walk your hands forward and fold over the front leg.
Flex the front foot to protect the knee and back off if you feel any knee pain; switch sides after the hold.

name: Bridge Pose
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet hip-width apart, heels close to your glutes and arms by your sides.
Press through your feet and arms to lift your hips, rolling your spine up one segment at a time.
Keep your knees pointing forward and your neck relaxed, without turning your head.
Hold, then roll down slowly from the upper back to the tailbone.

name: Happy Baby Pose
steps: Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your armpits.
Hold the outer edges of your feet, your ankles or your shins, with the soles facing the ceiling and shins vertical.
Gently pull down with your hands while pressing your feet up into them, keeping your back and head on the mat.
Rock gently side to side if it feels good.

name: Supine Spinal Twist
steps: Lie on your back, hug one knee into your chest and extend the other leg along the floor.
Guide the bent knee across your body toward the floor with the opposite hand.
Stretch the other arm out to the side and let that shoulder blade stay heavy, turning your gaze away from the knee if comfortable.
Breathe into the twist, then switch sides.

name: Seated Forward Fold
steps: Sit with your legs extended in front of you, on a folded blanket if your lower back rounds.
Inhale to lengthen your spine, then hinge forward from the hips.
Hold your shins, ankles or feet, or loop a strap around your feet, keeping your chest open.
Let the spine soften forward only after the hinge, and keep breathing slowly.

name: Standing Forward Fold
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hinge forward from the hips.
Bend your knees as much as needed to rest your belly on your thighs, and let your head and arms hang.
Slowly straighten your legs toward your edge without locking the knees.
To rise, bend your knees and roll up slowly.

name: Bound Angle Pose
steps: Sit tall with the soles of your feet together and knees falling out to the sides.
Hold your feet or ankles and draw your heels toward you to a comfortable distance.
Lengthen through your spine; for more stretch, hinge forward from the hips without forcing your knees down.

name: Garland Pose
steps: Stand with feet slightly wider than your hips and toes turned out.
Lower into a deep squat, keeping your heels down or resting them on a rolled mat if needed.
Bring your palms together at your chest and press your elbows gently against your inner knees to lengthen your spine.
Hold with your chest lifted, then press through your feet to stand.

name: Camel Pose
steps: Kneel with knees hip-width apart and your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Lift your chest and press your hips forward over your knees, drawing your elbows toward each other.
Bend back only as far as you can keep length in your lower back, reaching for your heels only if it is comfortable.
Come up slowly with your chin tucked, leading with your chest.

name: Boat Pose
steps: Sit with knees bent and feet on the floor, holding the backs of your thighs.
Lean back slightly with a long spine and lift your feet until your shins are parallel to the floor.
Release your hands and reach your arms forward; straighten your legs only if you can keep your chest lifted.
Hold while breathing steadily, then lower your feet with control.

name: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
steps: Sit with legs extended, bend one knee and place that foot on the floor outside the opposite knee.
Bend the bottom leg so its heel rests near the opposite hip, or keep it straight.
Inhale to sit tall, then exhale and rotate toward the bent knee, hooking the opposite elbow outside it and placing your other hand behind you.
Lengthen on each inhale and twist a little further on each exhale, then switch sides.

name: Thread the Needle Pose
steps: Start on hands and knees with hips over knees.
Slide one arm under your chest along the floor, palm up, lowering that shoulder and the side of your head to the mat.
Keep your hips square over your knees and let your upper back rotate.
Press the other hand into the floor or reach it overhead, hold, then switch sides.

name: Cow Face Pose
steps: Sit or stand tall and reach one arm overhead, then bend that elbow so the hand drops between your shoulder blades.
Reach the other arm out to the side, bend it behind your back and slide the hand up toward the top hand.
Clasp your fingers or hold a strap between your hands, keeping your head upright rather than pushed forward.
Hold, then switch arms.

name: Eagle Pose
steps: Stand with knees bent, lift one leg and cross that thigh over the other, hooking the foot behind the standing calf if possible.
Cross your arms at the elbows in front of you, bend them and bring the palms or the backs of the hands together.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height and draw them forward to stretch between your shoulder blades.
Sink your hips and hold, then switch sides.

name: Puppy Pose
steps: Start on hands and knees with hips stacked over knees.
Walk your hands forward and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your hips high above your knees.
Rest your forehead or chin on the mat and press your palms down while reaching your hips back to lengthen your spine.
Breathe into your upper back, then walk your hands back to come out.

name: Locust Pose
steps: Lie face down with arms by your sides, palms down and forehead on the mat.
Press the tops of your feet down, then lift your chest, arms and legs off the floor together.
Reach back through your fingertips and toes, keeping the back of your neck long and your gaze down.
Hold for a few breaths, then lower with control.

name: Legs Up the Wall
steps: Sit sideways next to a wall, then swing your legs up the wall as you lie back.
Shuffle your hips close to the wall, or slightly away if your hamstrings are tight, and rest your arms by your sides.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly for several minutes.
To come out, bend your knees, roll to one side and pause before sitting up.

name: Corpse Pose
steps: Lie on your back with legs extended and slightly apart, arms a little away from your body, palms up.
Let your feet fall open and close your eyes, letting the floor take your full weight.
Breathe naturally and relax each area of your body from feet to head.
To finish, deepen your breath, roll to one side and press up slowly.

name: Sun Salutation A
steps: From Mountain Pose, inhale and sweep your arms overhead, then exhale and fold forward.
Inhale to a half lift with a flat back, then exhale and step back to plank and lower to the floor, knees down if needed.
Inhale into Cobra or Upward-Facing Dog, then exhale back to Downward-Facing Dog for five breaths.
Step forward, inhale to a half lift, exhale to fold, then inhale to rise with arms overhead and return to Mountain Pose.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
steps: Sit on the floor with both knees bent to about 90 degrees and feet planted wider than your hips, hands behind you if needed.
Let both knees fall to one side so the front leg rotates outward and the back leg rotates inward.
Lift the knees and rotate them over to the other side, keeping your feet in place and chest tall.
Move slowly in a pain-free range; progress by removing the hand support.

name: Thoracic Open Book
steps: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, head on a cushion and arms straight in front of you, palms together.
Keep your knees stacked together, then sweep the top arm up and over to open your chest toward the ceiling.
Follow your hand with your eyes and let the arm settle toward the floor on the other side as you exhale.
Bring the arm back over the top slowly, repeat, then switch sides.

name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
steps: Start on hands and knees, then sit your hips back slightly toward your heels to keep your lower back still.
Place one hand behind your head.
Rotate that elbow down toward the opposite wrist, then up toward the ceiling as far as you can while your hips stay still.
Exhale at the top and follow the elbow with your eyes; switch sides after the set.

name: Cat-Cow
steps: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale as you let your belly drop, tilting your pelvis forward and lifting your chest and gaze (cow).
Exhale as you round your spine toward the ceiling, tucking your tailbone and chin (cat).
Move slowly through your whole spine, one segment at a time.

name: Shoulder CARs
steps: Stand tall, make a fist with one hand, and brace your core and glutes so your trunk stays still.
Raise the straight arm forward and overhead as high as you can, palm facing in.
Near the top, turn your palm to face outward and continue the circle back and down behind you, finishing with the palm facing back beside your hip.
Move slowly with control and reverse the direction on the next rep.

name: Hip CARs
steps: Stand on one leg holding a wall for support and brace your core so your pelvis does not move.
Lift the free knee toward your chest as high as you can.
Open the knee out to the side, then rotate your foot up and your knee back behind you as if stepping over a hurdle.
Bring the thigh back down beside the standing leg, moving as slowly as you can; reverse the direction on the next rep.

name: Wrist CARs
steps: Make a fist and grip your forearm just below the wrist with the other hand to keep the forearm still.
Slowly move the fist through the largest circle you can: down, toward the little finger, up, and toward the thumb.
Keep the forearm from rotating and make each circle slow and deliberate.
Complete the reps, then reverse the direction and switch hands.

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobilization
steps: Stand facing a wall in a split stance with your front toes a few centimetres from the wall.
Keeping your front heel down, drive your knee forward over your middle toes until it touches the wall.
Return and repeat; when it becomes easy, move the foot a little further back.
Do not let your arch collapse or your heel lift.

name: Quadruped Wrist Rocks
steps: Kneel on hands and knees with hands under your shoulders and fingers spread.
Rock your body gently forward and back over your hands to load the wrists in extension.
Turn your hands so the fingers point toward your knees and rock back to stretch the forearm flexors, then rest on the backs of your hands for the extensors.
Keep the pressure light and move only in a comfortable range.

name: Band Shoulder Pass-Through
steps: Hold a light band in front of your thighs with a wide grip and straight arms.
Brace your core and raise the band overhead and back behind you in one smooth arc until it reaches your lower back.
Reverse the arc to return to the front, keeping your elbows straight and ribs down.
Widen your grip if you feel pinching or need to bend your elbows.

name: Scapular Wall Slides
steps: Stand facing a wall and place the little-finger side of your forearms on it, elbows at shoulder height and slightly narrower than your shoulders.
Gently press your forearms into the wall so your shoulder blades wrap forward.
Slide your forearms up the wall into a Y as far as you can without shrugging, then lift them slightly off the wall for a second.
Return your forearms to the wall and slide back down slowly.

name: Squat-to-Stand
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hinge forward and grab your toes, bending your knees as needed.
Keeping hold of your toes, drop your hips into a deep squat with your chest lifted and elbows inside your knees.
Raise one arm, then the other, overhead to lift your chest.
Return your hands to your toes and straighten your legs to feel the hamstrings, then repeat.

name: Walking Leg Cradle
steps: Step forward and lift the other leg, holding the knee with one hand and the ankle with the other so the shin is roughly horizontal.
Draw the leg gently toward your chest while rising onto the toes of the standing foot.
Step forward and repeat with the other leg, keeping your torso upright.

name: Hip Airplane
steps: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend, holding a wall or support at first, and hinge forward until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
Keeping the standing knee still, rotate your pelvis open so the free hip turns toward the ceiling.
Rotate back and close your pelvis down toward the standing leg, moving through the hip rather than the lower back.
Move slowly for the set reps, then switch legs.

name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
steps: Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back just below the shoulder blades, knees bent and hands supporting your head.
Keep your hips on the floor and ribs down, then gently extend your upper back over the roller.
Pause, return to the start, and shift the roller up a few centimetres to work another segment.
Avoid rolling into your lower back or neck.

name: Frog Rocks
steps: Start on hands and knees, then widen your knees as far as is comfortable with the inner edges of your knees and feet on the floor and shins parallel.
Keep your spine neutral and slowly rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel a stretch in your inner thighs.
Rock forward to the start and repeat, pausing briefly at the end range.

name: Cossack Squat
steps: Stand with feet very wide and toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side and sit into a deep squat on that leg while the other leg straightens with its toes pointing up.
Keep the heel of the bent leg down and your chest up, using your hands in front for balance.
Push back through the middle and alternate sides.

name: Walking Knee Hug
steps: Step forward and lift the opposite knee toward your chest.
Grab just below the knee with both hands and hug it in while rising onto the toes of the standing leg.
Release, step through and repeat on the other side as you walk forward.

name: Chin Tucks
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and eyes looking straight ahead.
Glide your head straight back to make a double chin, without tipping your head up or down.
Hold for three seconds while feeling a gentle stretch at the base of your skull, then release.

name: Prone Swimmers
steps: Lie face down with your forehead on a towel and arms reaching overhead, thumbs up, hovering just off the floor.
Sweep your arms out to the sides and down toward your hips, rotating the palms to face up behind your back.
Reverse the path back overhead while keeping your hands off the floor and neck long.
Move slowly and shorten the range if your shoulders pinch.

name: Dowel Hip Hinge Drill
steps: Hold a dowel or broomstick along your spine so it touches the back of your head, upper back and tailbone.
Soften your knees and push your hips back, tilting your torso forward while keeping all three contact points on the stick.
Stop when you feel your hamstrings tighten or the stick starts to lose a contact point.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.

name: Racket Forearm Rotations
steps: Hold a tennis racket by the handle with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side, forearm resting on a table or your thigh if you like.
Start with the racket pointing straight up, then slowly turn your palm down until the racket is horizontal.
Rotate back through vertical and over to palm up, controlling the racket the whole way.
Choke up on the handle to make it easier, or hold nearer the end to add load.

name: Shin Box Get-Up
steps: Sit in a 90/90 position with your front shin across your body and your back shin out to the side.
Keeping your chest tall, press through the front shin and squeeze your glutes to rise up onto both knees.
Lower back to the seated 90/90 with control.
Switch your legs to the other side and repeat, using a hand for support at first.

name: Toy Soldiers
steps: Walk forward, kicking one straight leg up in front of you to a comfortable height while reaching the opposite hand toward the toes.
Keep your torso tall and the standing knee soft.
Lower the leg, step through and repeat with the other leg.

name: Forearm Ball Release
steps: Rest your forearm on a table and place a tennis or massage ball under the muscles just below your elbow.
Lean gently into the ball and roll slowly from below the elbow toward the wrist, pausing on tender spots for a few breaths.
Open and close your hand or rotate your forearm while pausing to add movement.
Keep the pressure moderate and avoid pressing directly on the bony point of the elbow.

name: Sleeper Stretch
steps: Lie on the side you want to stretch with that upper arm straight out in front at shoulder height and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, fingers pointing up.
Roll your body back slightly, about 20 to 30 degrees, so your shoulder blade is not trapped under you.
Use your other hand to gently press the forearm down toward the floor until you feel a stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Keep it gentle and stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

name: Doorway Pec Stretch
steps: Stand in a doorway and place one forearm on the frame with the elbow at or slightly below shoulder height.
Step through with the same-side foot and gently turn your chest away until you feel a stretch across the chest and front of the shoulder.
Keep your shoulder blade drawn back and down rather than shrugged forward.
Raise the elbow slightly higher to shift the stretch toward the lower chest fibres.

name: Standing Wrist Flexor Stretch
steps: Hold one arm straight in front of you at shoulder height with the palm facing up.
Use your other hand to gently pull the fingers down and back toward you.
Keep the elbow straight and feel the stretch along the inside of your forearm.

name: Standing Wrist Extensor Stretch
steps: Hold one arm straight in front of you at shoulder height with the palm facing down.
Use your other hand to gently bend the wrist down, drawing the back of the hand toward you.
For more stretch, make a loose fist first and keep the elbow straight; feel it along the top of your forearm.

name: Prayer Wrist Stretch
steps: Press your palms together in front of your chest with elbows out to the sides.
Keeping your palms together, slowly lower your hands toward your waist until you feel a stretch in your wrists and forearms.
Then turn the backs of your hands together with fingers pointing down and gently raise them for a reverse prayer stretch.

name: Couch Stretch
steps: Kneel with your back to a couch or wall and slide one shin up it so the knee sits in the corner and the top of the foot rests against the surface.
Step the other foot forward into a lunge with the foot flat.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck your pelvis slightly, then slowly lift your torso upright until you feel a strong stretch in the front of the thigh and hip.
Pad the knee and ease off if you feel any knee pain.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
steps: Sit tall and hold the edge of your chair with one hand to anchor that shoulder down.
Turn your head about 45 degrees away from the anchored side and look down toward your opposite armpit.
Place your free hand on the back of your head and add very light pressure until you feel a stretch from the neck to the top of the shoulder blade.

name: Kneeling Shin Stretch
steps: Kneel on a mat with the tops of your feet flat and toes pointing straight back.
Sit your hips back toward your heels, placing your hands beside your knees for support.
To deepen, lean back slightly and lift your knees a little off the floor until you feel a stretch along the front of your shins and ankles.
Place a folded towel under your ankles if this is too intense.

name: Seated Figure-Four Stretch
steps: Sit tall on a chair or bench with both feet flat, then cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Let the crossed knee drop toward the floor and keep the foot flexed to protect the knee.
Hinge forward from your hips with a long back until you feel a stretch deep in the outer hip.

name: Plantar Fascia Toe Stretch
steps: Sit and cross one foot over the opposite knee.
Hold your toes and gently pull them back toward your shin until you feel a stretch along the arch.
Use the thumb of your other hand to massage along the arch while holding the stretch.

name: Towel Shoulder Internal Rotation Stretch
steps: Hold a towel over one shoulder with the top hand and grab the lower end behind your back with the other hand.
Gently pull the towel upward with the top hand to slide the lower hand up your back.
Stop at a mild stretch in the front and side of the lower shoulder and keep your shoulders level.
Ease off immediately if you feel pinching or pain.

name: Step Heel Drop Calf Stretch
steps: Stand on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on the step and heels hanging off, holding a rail for balance.
Slowly let one or both heels sink below the step until you feel a stretch in your calves.
Hold with the knee straight, then repeat with a slight knee bend to target the lower calf and Achilles.

name: Half-Kneeling Adductor Stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg straight out to the side with the foot flat and toes pointing forward.
Keep your back flat with hands on the floor or your thighs.
Shift your hips back toward the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inner thigh of the straight leg.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
steps: Kneel facing a bench or couch and rest your elbows on its edge, shoulder-width apart, with palms together.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and let your chest sink toward the floor.
Bend your elbows to bring your hands behind your head for a deeper stretch through the lats and triceps.

name: Foam Roller Chest Opener
steps: Lie lengthwise on a foam roller so it supports your head and spine, knees bent and feet flat.
Let your arms fall out to the sides, palms up, in a T or slightly higher.
Relax and breathe, letting gravity open your chest; bend your elbows if your hands start to tingle.

name: Split-Step Drill
steps: Stand in an athletic ready position with feet just wider than hips and knees soft.
Take a small hop to unweight, landing on the balls of both feet slightly wider apart with knees bent, as if timing your opponent's contact.
On landing, immediately push off into a first step or shuffle left, right or forward, then recover to the centre.
Stay light and low; the quality of the landing matters more than speed.

name: Skater Jumps
steps: Stand on one leg in a quarter squat with your chest slightly forward.
Push off sideways and leap to land softly on the opposite foot, letting the trailing leg sweep behind the landing leg.
Absorb the landing with a bent knee that tracks over your toes, then immediately bound back.
Increase distance and speed only while landings stay quiet and controlled.

name: Lateral Shuffle
steps: Get into an athletic stance with feet wider than your hips, knees bent and chest up.
Push off the trailing foot to shuffle sideways, without letting your feet cross or click together.
Stay low with your head level for the set time, changing direction at each end.

name: Pogo Hops
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Bounce on the balls of your feet with stiff ankles and nearly straight knees, spending as little time on the ground as possible.
Keep the hops low and rhythmic; progress to side-to-side or single-leg pogos later.

name: Burpee
steps: From standing, squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank and lower your chest to the floor, or do a push-up.
Push up, then jump or step your feet back toward your hands.
Stand and jump with arms overhead, landing softly to start the next rep.

name: Jumping Jacks
steps: Stand with feet together and arms by your sides.
Jump your feet out wider than your hips while sweeping your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start with arms down, staying light on the balls of your feet.

name: High Knees
steps: Stand tall and run in place, driving each knee up to hip height.
Land on the balls of your feet and pump your arms in rhythm with your legs.
Keep your torso upright and core braced rather than leaning back.

name: Bear Crawl
steps: Start on hands and knees, then lift your knees a few centimetres off the floor with your back flat.
Crawl forward by moving the opposite hand and foot together in small steps.
Keep your hips low and level and your knees hovering throughout; crawl backward to return.

name: Lateral Lunge
steps: Stand with feet together, then take a wide step to one side.
Sit your hips back and bend the stepping knee, keeping the other leg straight and both feet flat and pointing forward.
Lower until the thigh is near parallel while keeping your chest up, then push off the bent leg to return.

name: Bodyweight Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Stand on one leg with a soft knee and arms by your sides.
Hinge forward at the hip while the free leg reaches straight back, keeping your hips square to the floor.
Lower until your torso and back leg are near parallel to the floor or you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive the standing hip forward to return to tall standing without touching down.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
steps: Stand on one foot on a step edge or the floor, lightly holding a wall for balance.
Rise as high as you can onto the ball of the foot, keeping the knee straight.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly over about three seconds, below step level if you are using a step.

name: Wall Sit
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and walk your feet out about two feet.
Slide down until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees, with knees over ankles.
Hold with your back flat against the wall and weight in your heels, breathing steadily.

name: Push-Up Plus
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders, or on your knees for an easier version.
Do a push-up, then at the top push the floor further away so your upper back rounds slightly and your shoulder blades spread apart.
Let your shoulder blades return to neutral and repeat, keeping your hips in line.

name: Shadow Forehand Swing
steps: Start in a ready position, split step, and turn your shoulders and hips together into a forehand unit turn.
Step into the shot and swing through a contact point in front of your body, rotating hips then shoulders.
Finish over the opposite shoulder in balance, then shuffle back to the centre.
Hold a racket or keep your hand empty, and focus on smooth rhythm and footwork at match speed.

name: Shadow Backhand Swing
steps: From a ready position, split step and turn your shoulders sideways so your back partly faces the net.
Step into the shot and swing from low to high through a contact point in front of your front hip.
Finish high in balance with your head still through contact, then recover to the centre.
Use your own backhand style, one-handed or two-handed, with or without a racket.

name: Shadow Serve
steps: Stand side-on at an imaginary baseline with your feet in your serving stance.
Raise your tossing arm and racket arm together into the trophy position, knees bent and shoulders tilted.
Drive up from your legs, rotate your trunk and reach up to an imaginary contact point, turning the forearm over through contact.
Land on your front foot and recover; start at half speed to warm the shoulder before going to full speed.

name: Rotational Shadow Throw
steps: Stand side-on in an athletic stance with your hands together at your back hip as if holding a medicine ball.
Load into the back hip, then drive your hips toward the target and let your trunk and arms whip through as if throwing a ball at a wall.
Finish with your chest facing the target and the back heel turned out, then reset.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch; make every rep fast and crisp.

name: 180-Degree Jump Squat
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat to a comfortable depth.
Jump explosively and rotate 180 degrees in the air using your arms and hips.
Land softly in a squat facing the opposite direction, knees tracking over your toes.
Alternate the direction of the turn on each rep.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder while keeping your hips still and level.
Return the hand and alternate sides at a slow, controlled pace.

name: Side Plank
steps: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked, or bend the bottom knee for an easier version.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Keep your hips stacked and pushed slightly forward rather than sagging or piking.
Hold for the set time, then switch sides.

name: Copenhagen Plank
steps: Lie on your side next to a bench and prop yourself up on your elbow, placing the top leg on the bench: knee on the bench for the short-lever version, inner ankle for the long-lever version.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line, letting the bottom leg hang or lifting it toward the bench.
Hold with your hips stacked while squeezing the top inner thigh down into the bench.
Start with the short-lever version and short holds if you are new to it.

name: Bird Dog
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders, knees under hips and spine neutral.
Brace your core and slowly reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso.
Pause for two seconds without letting your hips rotate or your lower back sag.
Return under control and alternate sides.
aliases: Quadruped Opposite Arm and Leg Raise

name: Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lie on your back and press your lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift your shoulders, arms and legs off the floor, arms reaching overhead and legs long, so your body forms a shallow banana shape.
Keep your lower back pinned; bend your knees or bring your arms forward to make it easier.
Hold while breathing steadily.

name: Plank Up-Down
steps: Start in a forearm plank with feet slightly wider than your hips.
Place one hand under your shoulder and press up, then the other, to reach a high plank.
Lower back to your forearms one arm at a time, alternating the lead arm each rep.
Keep your hips as still and level as possible throughout.

name: Cross-Body Mountain Climbers
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders.
Drive one knee toward the opposite elbow, then quickly switch legs.
Keep your hips low and shoulders over your wrists as you move at a steady, fast rhythm.

name: Glute Bridge March
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, then lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping your pelvis level, lift one foot a few centimetres off the floor and draw that knee toward your chest.
Lower it and repeat with the other leg without letting your hips drop or twist.

name: Side Plank Reach-Through
steps: Set up in a forearm side plank with hips lifted and your top arm reaching to the ceiling.
Rotate your chest toward the floor and thread the top arm under your body.
Rotate back open to reach to the ceiling, keeping your hips high and still.
Complete the reps, then switch sides.

name: Outdoor Run
steps: Start with five minutes of easy jogging or brisk walking to warm up.
Run at a conversational pace where you could still speak in short sentences, landing with your feet under your hips.
Keep your upper body relaxed and your steps quick and light rather than overstriding.
Finish with a few minutes of walking to cool down.

name: Sprint Intervals
steps: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy jogging plus a few short accelerations.
Sprint at about 90 percent effort for the work interval, staying tall and driving your arms.
Walk or jog slowly for the full rest period until your breathing settles.
Stop the session if your form breaks down or you feel a pull in a hamstring.

name: Brisk Walk
steps: Walk at a pace that raises your breathing but still lets you hold a conversation.
Stand tall, swing your arms naturally and roll from heel to toe.
Add hills or pick up the pace to raise the intensity.

name: Cycling Intervals
steps: Warm up with 5 to 10 minutes of easy pedalling.
Pedal hard for the work interval at a high cadence or resistance, then spin easily for the rest period.
Repeat for the set rounds, keeping the hard efforts consistent rather than fading.
Cool down with 5 minutes of easy spinning.

name: Rowing Intervals
steps: Strap your feet in and set the damper to a moderate level, around 3 to 5.
Drive with your legs first, then swing your torso back slightly and finish by pulling the handle to your lower ribs.
Return in reverse order: arms away, hinge forward from the hips, then bend your knees.
Row each interval at a hard but sustainable pace and rest fully between efforts.

name: Jump Rope Intervals
steps: Hold the handles at hip height with elbows close to your sides and turn the rope with your wrists.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Mix basic bounces with boxer skips or side-to-side hops to build footwork.
Rest between rounds and keep a steady rhythm rather than rushing.

name: Stair Climbing
steps: Find a flight of stairs and climb at a steady pace, placing your whole foot on each step.
Drive through the front heel and keep your torso upright, using the rail lightly for balance.
Walk down carefully to recover and repeat for the set time.
Progress to taking two steps at a time or adding faster climbs.

name: Freestyle Swimming
steps: Warm up with a few easy lengths of any stroke.
Swim front crawl with a long body line, rotating from your hips and breathing to the side every two or three strokes.
Reach forward with each arm and pull back under your body, finishing past your hip.
Rest at the wall as needed and keep an even pace.

name: Tennis Match Play
steps: Warm up first with a dynamic routine and 5 to 10 minutes of mini-tennis and groundstrokes.
Play sets or practice games, split-stepping as your opponent strikes the ball and recovering to position after every shot.
Drink regularly at changeovers.
Finish with easy movement and stretches for your forearms, shoulders and hips.

name: Tennis Spider Drill
steps: Place five balls or cones on the court: where each singles sideline meets the baseline, where each meets the service line, and at the T.
Starting at the centre mark of the baseline, sprint to one target, touch it or pick up the ball, and return to the centre.
Repeat for all five targets as fast as you can, using shuffles and crossover steps as you would in a rally.
Rest fully between rounds so every effort stays fast.

name: Agility Ladder Drills
steps: Lay an agility ladder flat on the ground.
Move through it with quick, light steps using patterns such as two feet in each square, lateral in-and-out or the Icky Shuffle.
Stay on the balls of your feet with arms pumping and eyes up as much as possible.
Make clean foot placement the priority, then build speed.

name: Tennis Court Sprints
steps: Start on the baseline at one doubles sideline.
Sprint to the near singles sideline and back, then to the centre mark and back, then to the far singles sideline and back.
Plant and change direction by bending your knees and lowering your hips rather than leaning or skidding.
Rest fully between rounds.
